bib.title: PubMedQA: A Dataset for Biomedical Research Question Answering
bib.venue: Proceedings of EMNLP-IJCNLP 2019, pages 2567-2577, Hong Kong

question: Can a biomedical QA dataset be built from PubMed question-titled abstracts that has expert labels and requires reasoning over quantitative research text to answer yes/no/maybe?
hypothesis: Pre-training on a large automatically labeled set and bootstrapping on pseudo-labeled unlabeled data, plus long-answer supervision, helps a low-resource, reasoning-heavy task.
contributions: PubMedQA: 1k expert-annotated, 61.2k unlabeled and 211.3k artificially generated yes/no/maybe QA instances from PubMed abstracts
Two evaluation settings: reasoning-required (question + context) and reasoning-free (question + long answer)
Multi-phase fine-tuning of BioBERT with long-answer bag-of-words auxiliary supervision as a baseline, compared with single-human performance

method.summary: Collect PubMed articles with question titles and structured abstracts; context is the abstract without its conclusion, long answer is the conclusion. Two M.D. candidates label 1k instances (PQA-L) with yes/no/maybe; the rest of the answerable ones form PQA-U; statement titles converted to questions form PQA-A. Baselines (majority, shallow features, BiLSTM, ESIM+BioELMo, BioBERT) are trained under several schedules.

datasets.name: PQA-L (labeled)
datasets.split: 500 randomly sampled instances for 10-fold cross-validation (450 train per fold), remaining 500 are the test set
datasets.source: PubMed articles with question-mark titles and structured abstracts with conclusion; labeled by two M.D. candidates
datasets.preprocessing: Annotator 1 sees question, context and long answer (reasoning-free); annotator 2 sees question and context only (reasoning-required); disagreements discussed, instance dropped if no agreement

datasets.name: PQA-U (unlabeled)
datasets.split: pseudo-labeled subset with same yes/no/maybe proportions as PQA-L used in Phase II
datasets.source: pre-PQA-U instances that are yes/no/maybe answerable
datasets.preprocessing: Rule-based removal of wh-questions and multi-entity selection questions; over 93% agreement with annotator 1 on answerability

datasets.name: PQA-A (artificial)
datasets.split: 200k randomly sampled for training, 11.3k for validation
datasets.source: PubMed articles with statement titles (NP-(VBP/VBZ) by Stanford CoreNLP) and structured abstract with conclusion
datasets.preprocessing: Statement title converted to question by moving or adding copulas or auxiliary verbs; label by negation status of the verb

models.name: BioBERT
models.init_from: BERT, further pre-trained on PubMed abstracts and PMC articles

other.input: question and context (or long answer) separated by [SEP]

models.name: ESIM with BioELMo
models.architecture: biLSTM encoder, attentional local inference, biLSTM composition, softmax; BioELMo weights fixed

models.name: BiLSTM
models.architecture: biLSTM over biomedical word2vec plus segment embeddings

models.name: Shallow Features
models.architecture: feed-forward net on TF-IDF of question, TF-IDF of context/long answer, summed IDF of overlapping non-stop words

training.objective: L = L_QA + beta * L_BoW; L_QA cross-entropy on yes/no/maybe, L_BoW binary cross-entropy predicting binary bag-of-words of the long answer from [CLS] (beta = 0 in reasoning-free setting)

other.schedule: Phase I: fine-tune on PQA-A (question, context). Bootstrapping: fine-tune on PQA-A (question, long answer), then PQA-L (question, long answer), pseudo-label PQA-U with the most confident predictions per class in PQA-L proportions. Phase II: fine-tune on pseudo-labeled PQA-U (question, context). Final: fine-tune on PQA-L (question, context).
other.compared_schedules: Final Phase Only, Single-phase (combined PQA-A + bootstrapped PQA-U + PQA-L), Phase I + Final, Phase II + Final, Multi-phase

inference.decoding: argmax over softmax of 3 classes (inferred from classification setup)

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction of PQA-L test instances with correct yes/no/maybe label, question and context as input

metrics.name: Macro-F1
metrics.definition: macro-averaged F1 over yes/no/maybe on the PQA-L test set

eval.protocol: Test on 500 PQA-L instances; 10-fold cross-validation on the other 500 for validation. Human performance measured during annotation, single annotator against discussed ground truth. Single run per cell reported; no seeds or significance tests stated.

evidence.quote: 500 randomly sampled PQA-L instances are used for 10-fold cross validation and the rest 500 instances consist of Pub- MedQA test set.

results.setup: PQA-L test set, reasoning-required setting, BioBERT multi-phase with additional supervision
results.table: Table 5, row BioBERT w/ A.S., column Multi-phase Acc

results.claim: Dataset sizes: 1k expert-annotated, 61.2k unlabeled, 211.3k artificially generated instances.
results.quote: PubMedQA has 1k expert-annotated, 61.2k unlabeled and 211.3k artiﬁcially gen- erated QA instances.

results.claim: About half of the question-titled candidates are unanswerable by yes/no/maybe.
results.setup: manual answerability screen at start of PQA-L annotation
results.quote: We labeled 1091 (about 50.2%) of 2173 question titles as unanswerable.

results.claim: Estimated error rate of ground-truth labels could be as low as 1%.
results.setup: roughly half of the product of two annotator error rates (footnote 4)
results.quote: such error rate could be as low as 1%

results.quote: Reasoning over quantitative con- tents is required in nearly all (96.5%) of them
results.note: 75.5% of contexts have text descriptions of the statistics, 21.0% numbers only, 3.5% no numbers

results.claim: Yes/no-answerable question titles are common in PubMed versus other datasets.
results.source: Kwiatkowski et al. 2019 (Natural Questions); Yang et al. 2018 (HotpotQA)
results.setup: compared with more than half of PubMed question titles
results.quote: just 1% in Natural Questions (Kwiatkowski et al., 2019) and 6% in HotpotQA (Yang et al., 2018)

limits: Human performance is single-annotator only, a lower bound by authors' admission.
Ground truth could be wrong if both annotators make the same mistake (estimated about 1%).
PQA-A labels are heuristic and very imbalanced (92.8% yes, 0% maybe); Phase II results are not comparable across models because each uses its own pseudo-labels.
Topics skew to clinical-study subjects (Appendix B).
Yes/no/maybe labelling is context-dependent: 'yes' means the paper's results indicate it (Appendix C), not universal truth.
Optimizer, learning rate, batch size, epochs, beta, seeds and hardware are not stated, so baseline training is not reproducible from the paper.
Task is 3-way classification, so a 55.2% majority baseline and a 500-instance test set give wide uncertainty; no confidence intervals or seeds reported.
Predates LLMs; baseline numbers are BERT-era.

terms.definition: prediction using question and context; answers are not directly expressed in the input
models use question and long answer to predict yes/no/maybe, since the label is usually explicit in the conclusion
the conclusion of the abstract, which presumably answers the research question
